To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best tilt/translations ratios for the simulation of decelaration and acceleration are not the same.
the perception of longitudinal acceleration depends on the level (level of acceleration) but not on the tilt/translation ratio (ratio of tilt/translation).
the best tilt/ translation ratios for braking and acceleration on a driving simulator are not the same.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the simulation of the perception of motion in a dynamic driving simulator.
a better understanding of how the human senses perceive motion.
the design of a driving simulator that can be used to study the human response to driving situations that may lead to accidents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best tilt/ translation ratio for the simulation braking during a passive driving task is a ratio of 1.5:1 for a deceleration level between 1 and 4 m/s2.
for deceleration a tilt/translation ratio of 1.5:1 is the most realistic for the simulation of deceleraion on a driving simulator.
for deceleration the most realistic tilt to translation ratio is 0.8 for 2G deceleration, and 0.6 for 4G deceleration.
